summary: AI-Scientist builds every LLM client in one factory (ai_scientist/llm.py:create_client) plus five hand-rolled constructions in the three entry points, and runs a sixth path through aider/LiteLLM for the experiment coder and the LaTeX writeup. I wrapped the Anthropic and OpenAI clients in the factory, the four reviewer clients and the one Anthropic client built outside it, and added install_litellm() so aider's OpenAI-provider calls route per request; all of it is inert until RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY is set. Two things blocked the traffic that mattered: every GPT request carries seed=0, which Router's /v1/responses rejects, and the models the app ships (claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 as the default --model, gpt-4o-2024-05-13 hardcoded in the reviewer, the o1/o3 family) are not Router catalog ids, so the runtime kept them on the vendor. router.policy.json now drops seed on the two LLM helpers and maps the retired ids to their nearest current catalog model, which is the one place a human can undo the model change. Verified live against real Router: the reviewer path served 200 on /v1/responses as gpt-4.1-mini and the default idea-generation path 200 on /v1/messages as claude-sonnet-4-6. The DeepSeek, OpenRouter and Gemini clients point at other vendors' hosts and stay there; the review ensemble's n=5 request and aider's Anthropic traffic also stay, and each has a ranked item saying what it would take.
reviewed: I read every LLM call path: the llm.py dispatcher and its nine call sites, generate_ideas (ideas, 3 reflections each, novelty check against Semantic Scholar), perform_writeup (per-section drafting plus citation search), perform_review (5-sample ensemble, 5 reflections, meta-review), perform_experiments (aider only), the two launchers and review_iclr_bench's inline copy of create_client, then traced each one through the runtime against the simulator and twice against real Router. The proposals below are ranked by how much of a run's cost or failure risk they touch: aider is the largest token consumer, the review ensemble the largest single-call fan-out, and provider failure the thing that actually ends 12-hour runs today (the app's only answer is an unbounded backoff loop on two exception types).

items.title: Route the shared Anthropic and OpenAI clients
items.summary: create_client's Anthropic and OpenAI constructions go through the vendored runtime, so every call in llm.py routes per request.
items.gains: One gateway and one key for idea generation, novelty checks, the LaTeX writeup, citation search and paper review - the whole research loop except aider.
items.price: no change (the runtime routes per request and falls back to the provider)
items.why: create_client is the single factory the whole codebase imports, so one wrap at each construction covers all nine call sites the scanner sees. The Bedrock and Vertex clients are left alone: they carry the caller's own cloud credentials and the runtime would not route them anyway.

evidence.detail: check --run over a probe that drives create_client + get_response_from_llm: gpt and o-series requests arrived at router-sim /v1/responses, the Claude path at /v1/messages
check --run --live: 2 requests, 2 ok - 200 /v1/responses model=gpt-4.1-mini provider=openai, 200 /v1/messages model=claude-sonnet-4-6 provider=anthropic
compileall + the six module imports: 10 passed

items.title: Drop seed=0 so the GPT paths route
items.summary: router.policy.json drops seed on the two LLM helpers, because Router's /v1/responses returns 400 for it.
items.gains: Every GPT and o-series call in llm.py becomes routable; without this the runtime kept all of them on OpenAI ("untranslatable: seed").
items.loses: seed=0 is no longer sent on routed calls, so repeated runs of the same prompt vary more than before (OpenAI treats seed as best-effort, and nothing in the app reads system_fingerprint or asserts on determinism).
items.why: The app sets seed=0 in three places to make runs comparable. Responses has no seed field at all, so the choice is between determinism-on-a-best-effort-basis and routing. The original request still goes to OpenAI untouched on the runtime's provider-fallback path, and ROUTER_MIGRATE_POLICY=off restores the old behaviour without a code change.

evidence.detail: before: all three sites reported stays "untranslatable: seed"; after: check --all shows them routing and router-sim received them

items.title: Map the pinned 2024 models to catalog ids
items.summary: The retired ids in AVAILABLE_LLMS are served by their nearest current Router catalog model.
items.gains: The default --model (claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620) and the reviewer's hardcoded gpt-4o-2024-05-13 reach Router at all; with the clients wrapped but no map, only a run with --model gpt-4o-mini or gpt-4.1-mini routed. Input price per 1M falls from $3 to $3 (Sonnet 3.5 -> claude-sonnet-4-6, unchanged) and from gpt-4o's $2.50/$10 to gpt-4.1-mini's $0.40/$1.60.
items.loses: answers will differ: a different model writes the ideas, the paper and the reviews. Sonnet 3.5 -> claude-sonnet-4-6 is a same-family successor at the same price; gpt-4o -> gpt-4.1-mini is a smaller model, and reviewer scores on the ICLR benchmark should be re-measured before anyone trusts the old numbers. o1/o1-mini/o3-mini -> gpt-5.1/gpt-5-mini keeps reasoning-model behaviour.
items.price: cheaper for the OpenAI paths (-84% in and -84% out vs gpt-4o), unchanged for Claude
items.why: Router serves only catalog ids, and none of the 2024-pinned ids the app ships are in the live catalog. Mapping is the only way this app's real traffic reaches Router, and keeping it in router.policy.json rather than in AVAILABLE_LLMS means the human can undo this one commit and keep every other routing decision. I chose non-reasoning, temperature-accepting targets for the gpt-4o family because llm.py always sends temperature and max_tokens=4096 and parses JSON out of the text; a reasoning target can spend that budget on thinking and return nothing.

evidence.detail: live: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 served 200 as gpt-4.1-mini on /v1/responses; claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 served 200 as claude-sonnet-4-6 on /v1/messages, response.model = claude-sonnet-4-6
router-migrate levers: claude-sonnet-4-6 $3/$15 (= Sonnet 3.5), gpt-4.1-mini $0.40/$1.60, gpt-5-mini $0.25/$2, gpt-5.1 $1.25/$10
no offline measure of review or idea quality exists in this repo; a paired run of review_iclr_bench on the old and new reviewer model would settle it

items.title: Route the reviewer clients built outside the factory
items.summary: The four openai.OpenAI() constructions in the two launchers and the inline client pair in review_iclr_bench go through the runtime.
items.gains: Paper review, the review after improvement and the ICLR benchmark harness route too; these are the calls create_client never sees, since the launchers build a client inline and iclr_analysis.py copies the dispatch.
items.why: perform_review is called with its own client, so wrapping create_client alone would have left every review on OpenAI - 5 ensemble samples plus 5 reflections plus a meta-review per paper, twice when --improvement is on.

evidence.detail: check --all: 7 of 9 scanner-visible calls route; the review path's requests reached router-sim through the same llm.py helpers
10 passed (compileall + imports)

items.title: Route aider's coder calls through LiteLLM
items.summary: install_litellm() at both launchers puts aider's OpenAI-provider traffic on Router per request.
items.gains: The experiment coder and the LaTeX writeup - the largest token consumer in a run, several hundred thousand tokens per idea - route when the run uses a GPT model, including through the model map (aider asking for gpt-4o-2024-05-13 was served as gpt-4.1-mini).
items.why: perform_experiments and perform_writeup drive aider, which reaches providers through LiteLLM rather than through any client this codebase builds; the runtime's LiteLLM hook is the only way to see that traffic without forking aider. It is a no-op without RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY and idempotent, so calling it per idea is safe under the multiprocessing worker (spawned children never run the __main__ block).

evidence.detail: check --run over a probe calling litellm.completion after install_litellm(): gpt-4o-2024-05-13 reached router-sim /v1/responses as gpt-4.1-mini; claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 went to api.anthropic.com (LiteLLM's Anthropic provider does not use client_session) - see i3

items.title: DeepSeek and OpenRouter clients stay on their vendors
items.summary: Those clients point at api.deepseek.com and openrouter.ai, and their model ids are not catalog ids, so their traffic is unchanged.
items.loses: Nothing is lost - these paths behave exactly as before - but their spend stays outside Router's reporting.
items.why: Routing another vendor's OpenAI-compatible host needs unlock_hosts plus a model map (deepseek-chat -> deepseek-v4-flash, llama3.1-405b -> an open-weight catalog id), which changes both the vendor and the model. That is a customer-approved decision, not a migration default, so it is proposed as i4. Note that `router-migrate check --all` optimistically reports llm.py:248/263/276 as routing: the scanner links those calls to the wrapped client in create_client, but at runtime the request goes to a host the runtime does not touch.

evidence.detail: probe with --model deepseek-chat / llama3.1-405b: requests left for the vendor host, no router-sim traffic

items.title: Gemini keeps its own endpoint
items.summary: The Gemini client talks to generativelanguage.googleapis.com, and Router's Gemini ids need the caller's own Vertex key.
items.loses: Nothing changes for --model gemini-*; that spend stays outside Router.
items.why: Router's gemini ids are Vertex BYOK entries (403 provider_key_required without a caller-owned credential), so pointing this client at Router would buy reporting only if the deployment has a Vertex key configured, and would change the model id too (gemini-1.5-flash and the 2.0 ids are not in the catalog).

evidence.detail: router-migrate levers: every gemini id is listed under vertex; ROUTER.md section 4 records 403 provider_key_required without a provider key

items.title: The Claude path is broken by the installed SDK
items.summary: anthropic 1.13.0's messages.create() has no temperature parameter, so llm.py's Claude branch raises TypeError before any request is built.
items.why: This is pre-existing and independent of Router: with the default --model claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620, get_response_from_llm dies with "Messages.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'temperature'" on the pinned SDK in this environment. I left the call as the app wrote it (a fix is a product decision about sampling, not a migration), and verified the wrap separately by calling the same wrapped client without temperature: it reached Router's /v1/messages as claude-sonnet-4-6, live. So the Anthropic routing is in place and starts working the moment that call is fixed - note that several current Claude models (Sonnet 5, every *-5-5, Opus 4.7+) reject temperature on Router as well, so the fix should drop it rather than re-add it.

evidence.detail: TypeError reproduced with no Router involvement; anthropic 1.13.0, openai 2.20.0
the same wrapped client without temperature: 200 /v1/messages model=claude-sonnet-4-6 provider=anthropic

items.title: Sample the review ensemble in parallel
items.summary: Replace the n=5 request in get_batch_responses_from_llm with one request per sample, run concurrently.
items.gains: The 5-sample paper-review ensemble routes (Router's /v1/responses has no `n`, so today the runtime keeps that request on OpenAI - it is the one call the migration cannot move), every provider takes the same code path, and the Claude ensemble stops being five sequential calls: wall clock for a 5-review ensemble drops from 5 round trips to about 2 (the first sample runs inline to warm the runtime's policy load, the rest in a pool of 4).
items.loses: The prompt is billed once per sample instead of once per batch. For the reviewer's roughly 10k-token prompt on gpt-4.1-mini that is 5 x $0.004 instead of 1 x $0.004 in input; with i2's prompt_cache_key the repeats read from cache at $0.10 per 1M instead of $0.40, so about 2x the input cost, not 5x. Sampling diversity may also differ slightly from one n=5 call.
items.price: about +$0.012 per ensemble on gpt-4.1-mini (+2x input, output unchanged), in exchange for moving that call onto Router
items.why: This is the only call site the migration leaves on the provider for a reason other than vendor choice, and it is the biggest single fan-out in the app. Independent samples are exactly what a thread pool is for; the batched form only ever existed because OpenAI's Chat Completions offered `n`. I also found a benign race while testing it: the runtime marks its policy loaded before it finishes importing it, so a cold concurrent burst can send the first requests to the provider. Running the first sample inline avoids that, and the comment in the code says why.

evidence.detail: check --run: all 3 samples of an n=3 ensemble reached router-sim as gpt-4.1-mini, none kept on the provider (before the inline-warmup fix, 1 of 4 leaked to the provider)
10 passed on the branch

items.title: Prompt cache keys and spend labels
items.summary: A per-feature prompt_cache_key and product/stage metadata on the research loop's Router-bound requests.
items.gains: Idea generation sends the same long prefix 1 + 3 reflections deep per idea, and each review 1 + 5 reflections deep over the same paper text; a stable cache key lets the provider read that prefix from cache. Measured on Router: a 9,020-token gpt-4o-mini prompt cost $0.00069 instead of $0.00135 on the second call (-49%), and Claude over Responses -90% with a key versus nothing without one. Labels make per-stage spend visible in Router's reporting without touching app code.
items.loses: nothing (prompt_cache_key only affects cache affinity and routing stickiness; metadata is recorded, not forwarded to the model)
items.price: cheaper on every repeated prefix; no added cost
items.why: Reflections are the dominant shape of this app's traffic and they are perfectly cacheable - same system prompt, same paper, one more turn. It is three lines of policy, applies only to Router-bound requests, and is undone by reverting one commit. It does not help the Claude path, which goes over /v1/messages where Router applies no policy fields; that needs i5.

evidence.detail: planned Router body for the reviewer's request: {model: gpt-4.1-mini, prompt_cache_key: "ai_scientist/llm.py:get_response_from_llm", metadata: {feature: ..., product: ai-scientist}} with seed dropped
ROUTER.md 6.3 measurements: -49% on gpt-4o-mini with a 9k prompt, -90% on Claude over Responses
10 passed on the branch

items.title: Run aider's Claude coder on Router
items.summary: Point LiteLLM's Anthropic provider at Router's /v1/messages and name a catalog model, so the coder's Claude traffic routes too.
items.gains: With the default --model, aider is both the biggest token consumer in a run and the last path still going straight to Anthropic; LiteLLM's Anthropic handler does not use the client_session the runtime installs (measured: that request left for api.anthropic.com). Router serves the Anthropic Messages API natively, so an api_base pointing at Router plus a catalog model id moves all of it, and the run's whole spend lands under one key.
items.loses: Per-request provider fallback for that path: once aider talks to Router directly, a Router error is aider's error rather than something the runtime can retry on Anthropic. The coder model also has to be named as a catalog id, which means a different model writes the experiment code (answers will differ), and aider's own cost accounting reads LiteLLM's price table, not Router's.
items.price: claude-sonnet-4-6 at $3/$15 is the same price as the Sonnet 3.5 aider uses today; claude-haiku-5-5 at $0.10/$0.50 would be 97% cheaper for the mechanical diff edits, at some cost in edit quality
items.why: Everything else in the app now routes; this is the remaining hole, and it is the expensive one. It needs a run of the real coder loop to be trusted (aider's diff format is sensitive to the model), which is why I propose it rather than ship it: a branch that changes how the coder is constructed without an end-to-end aider run would be a guess.

evidence.detail: probe: litellm.completion(claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620) after install_litellm() went to api.anthropic.com, confirming the gap
needs an aider coder run against Router's /v1/messages

items.title: Fail over across vendors instead of retrying forever
items.summary: Give the research loop's features a Router fallback list so a provider outage is answered rather than retried.
items.gains: Today the app's entire answer to provider failure is @backoff.on_exception(expo) on RateLimitError and APITimeoutError with no ceiling: a 429 storm makes a 12-hour run sleep instead of progress, and anything else (500, 503, overloaded_error - which the example aider logs in this repo show happening) ends the idea. A `fallbacks` list in router.policy.json makes Router try the next candidate inside the same request, cross-vendor (gpt-4.1-mini then claude-sonnet-4-6 was measured working in both directions).
items.loses: A different model may answer a given call mid-run, with no field in the response saying a fallback happened - so a paper can be part-written by two models and nothing records which. Flex and fallbacks do not combine (a list is served at the standard tier), so a Flex-eligible model loses its 50% discount on those requests; truncated attempts are still billed.
items.price: the serving candidate's price, only when it serves; the standard tier instead of Flex on those requests
items.why: This app runs unattended for hours and its failure mode is silent stalling, which is the worst kind for a research run. I did not ship it because the loses are real and the ranking between "one model wrote the paper" and "the run finished" is the owner's call, not mine. Either policy or a `models` list on a ported Responses call would do it; policy is the smaller change.

evidence.detail: ROUTER.md 6.2: up to 15 candidates on /v1/responses, falls through 403/404/invalid-parameter silently, cross-vendor measured; fallback on real provider 5xx/429 is documented but not measured

items.title: Pick the model per task, not per run
items.summary: Replace the one global --model and llm.py's substring dispatch with a per-task model choice on one Responses call path.
items.gains: A run currently sends one model to tasks with wildly different difficulty: generating a research idea, deciding whether a Semantic Scholar hit makes an idea unnovel, extracting a bibtex key, drafting a LaTeX section, and scoring a paper. On Router those can be different catalog ids with no new SDK, and the cheap ones are 10-30x cheaper (claude-haiku-5-5 $0.10/$0.50 or gpt-5-nano $0.05/$0.40 against claude-sonnet-4-6 $3/$15). The novelty check alone is up to 10 search-and-decide rounds per idea on 50 ideas. Porting the call path to /v1/responses also makes every Router lever reachable inline - fallbacks, Flex on the eligible OpenAI models (-50% measured on gpt-5.4-mini), provider_timeout, a cache key per task - instead of through a policy file, and the branching in get_response_from_llm (six near-identical blocks keyed on substrings like 'o1' in model, which also matches any model whose name happens to contain it) collapses to one request shape.
items.loses: A substantial rewrite of llm.py and its callers, and answers will differ per task. The app would commit to Responses, so the DeepSeek, OpenRouter and Gemini direct clients would either move to catalog ids or need to be kept as a separate path. Chat Completions' `n` and `seed` disappear for good (see i1, t1).
items.price: roughly -70% on the cheap-task share of a run if the mechanical tasks move to a nano/haiku-class model; no change on the generative ones
items.why: If I were starting this app on Router today I would not write a client factory at all: I would write one function that takes a task name, look the model up in config, and send it to /v1/responses with that task's levers. The current shape - one --model for everything, string-sniffing dispatch, a hand-rolled retry decorator, an ensemble built on `n` - is all workarounds for having two vendor SDKs and no gateway. This is the conversation worth having after the cheap wins land.

evidence.detail: router-migrate levers: claude-haiku-5-5 $0.10/$0.50, gpt-5-nano $0.05/$0.40, claude-sonnet-4-6 $3/$15; ROUTER.md 6.1: Flex -50% measured on gpt-5.4-mini

items.title: Bound a hung provider call
items.summary: Add provider_timeout to the research loop's features so a stuck request fails in minutes, not after the SDK's 10.
items.gains: No call in this app sets a timeout, so a hung generation blocks a run for the openai SDK's full 600s default (and aider's own default beyond that) before backoff even sees it. provider_timeout caps the provider attempt per request.
items.loses: A Router timeout comes back as a plain-text 504 with no JSON body, and 504 is not in the app's backoff tuple (RateLimitError, APITimeoutError): after the SDK's own retries that becomes an unhandled APIStatusError and the idea fails instead of hanging. So this should land together with either i4 (a fallback candidate answers) or a widened backoff/except clause - which is why it is a proposal, not a one-line commit.
items.price: no change; a timed-out attempt is still billed
items.why: Worth doing, but only with the error handling it implies. On its own it converts a slow run into a failed one, which is not an improvement.

evidence.detail: ROUTER.md 6.5: timeouts return a plain-text 504 with no x-request-id and the runtime passes them back to the app; max 660s

items.title: Serve the open-weight models from Router
items.summary: Unlock the DeepSeek and OpenRouter hosts and map their ids to Router's provider-agnostic catalog entries.
items.gains: The two cheap-model paths join the one key and one bill, and get Router's cross-provider routing for free: deepseek-chat/-coder/-reasoner map onto deepseek-v4-flash ($0.13/$0.26) or deepseek-v4-pro ($1.32/$3.96), and llama3.1-405b onto an open-weight id such as gpt-oss-120b ($0.15/$0.60) or nemotron-3-ultra ($0.60/$2.40). Two vendor keys (DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) stop being needed for those runs.
items.loses: answers will differ (different model generations, and Router may serve an open-weight id from a different provider on each turn - measured switching provider mid tool-loop). Token accounting on Messages is known-wrong for some Fireworks-served ids. Routing another vendor's host is an unlock the customer has to approve.
items.price: comparable or cheaper per token; exact comparison depends on which target is chosen
items.why: These are the paths people pick to run AI-Scientist cheaply, so leaving them off Router leaves the cost-sensitive runs unmeasured. It is a small change (one unlock_hosts argument plus map entries) but it changes vendor as well as model, so it belongs to the human.

evidence.detail: ROUTER.md 4 and 11: unlock_hosts routes another vendor's OpenAI-compatible host for catalog models only; open-weight ids can change provider per turn
